We define the \emph{derived category of $G$-representations} with coefficients in $R$ as the small stable $\infty$-category
\[
\mathrm{rep}(G,R) = \mathrm{Fun}(BG,\mathrm{Perf}(R)).

For example, based on H.~Krause's stable derived category \cite{krause_stablederived}, Balmer and Gallauer \cite{balmergallauer_permutationmodulescohomsing} have studied a version that agrees with the homotopy category of $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$. \mathrm{stmod}(G,R) \simeq \mathrm{rep}(G,R)/\Thickt{R[G]}.
\]
This recovers the definition of the stable module category given in \cite{krause_picard}, where even ring spectrum coefficients are permitted.

Therefore, viewed as a subspace of Spc(rep(G,R)), the Balmer spectrum Spc(stmod(G,R)) is the complement of supp(R[G]). The comparison map identifies the support of R[G] with its cohomological support. But End_rep(G,R)^*(R[G]) is isomorphic to R[G] concentrated in degree 0. By construction (see \cref{def:stmod}), $\mathrm{stmod}(G,R)$ is a finite localization of $\mathrm{rep}(G,R)$, away from the thick tensor ideal generated by $R[G]$. Therefore, viewed as a subspace of $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R))$, the Balmer spectrum $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(G,R))$ is the complement of $\mathrm{supp}(R[G])$. The comparison map \eqref{eq:laucomparisonmap} identifies the support of $R[G]$ with its cohomological support. But $\mathrm{End}_{\mathrm{rep}(G,R)}^*(R[G])$ is isomorphic to $R[G]$ concentrated in degree $0$. Since $R[G]$ is finite and free over $R$, we compute
\[
supp_{coh}(R[G]) = \SET{\frak p \in \mathrm{Spec}^h(H^*(G;R))}{H^{>0}(G;R) \subseteq \frak p}. 
\]
It follows that $\mathrm{supp}(R[G])$ identifies with $\mathrm{Spec}(R)$, as desired.

If $R=k$ is a field of characteristic $p$, then \cref{cor:spcstmod} recovers a theorem of Benson, Carlson, and Rickard \cite{BensonCarlsonRickard97}: The support variety of $G$ over $k$ is given by 
\[
\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(G,k)) \cong \mathrm{Proj}(H^*(G;k)).
\]

To see that the top right square commutes as well, one can either directly verify the dual Beck--Chevellay condition to establish the right adjointability of the left square. Likewise, f^*R[G] cong S[G], so the right square of commutes as well.

The individual components of the restriction functors were shown to be finite \'etale extensions of finite degree in \cref{prop:restrictionetale}. Since $\cat E(G)$ is finite, $\mathrm{res}$ is also finite \'etale of finite degree, and it remains to prove conservativity. 

To this end, note that Carlson's theorem \cref{thm:carlson} implies that there exist modules $W_E \in \mathrm{rep}(G,\mathbb{Z})$ for each $E \in \cat E(G)$ such that
\[
\mathbb{Z} \in \mathrm{Thick}(\SET{i_*W_E}{i\colon E \subseteq G, E \in \cat E(G)}).
\]
Thanks to the compatibility of coinduction with base-change (\cref{prop:basechangecompatibilities}), we obtain modules $V_E = R\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}W_E \in \mathrm{rep}(G,R)$ with 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gencarlson}
    R \in \mathrm{Thick}(\SET{i_*V_E}{i\colon E \subseteq G, E \in \cat E(G)}).
\end{equation}
Now consider $X \in \mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ with $\mathrm{res}(X) = 0$, so $i^!X \simeq 0$ for each elementary abelian subgroup $i\colon E \subseteq G$. It follows from the projection formula~\eqref{eq:projformula} that 
\[
0 \simeq X \otimes i_*V_E \simeq i_*(i^*(X)\otimes V_E)
\]
for all $E \in \cat E(G)$. Therefore, $X \otimes V \simeq 0$ for every $V \in \mathrm{Thick}(\SET{i_*V_E}{i\colon E \subseteq G, E \in \cat E(G)})$, hence $X \simeq X \otimes R \simeq 0$ by \cref{eq:gencarlson}. This concludes the proof.

\[
\xymatrix{A^{tE} \ar[r]^-{p^r} & A^{tE} \ar[r] & (A/p^r)^{tE}}
\]
in $\mathrm{Mod}(A^{tE})$. According to \cref{lem:elabtatecohom}, multiplication by $p^r$ is null on $A^{tE}$, so the above cofiber sequence exhibits $A^{tE}$ as a retract of $(A/p^r)^{tE}$.

The standard inclusion Econg (Z/p)^times r to (S^1)^times r induces a morphism of commutative ring spectra k^t(S^1)^times r to k^tE. Let $\alpha\colon A \to k$ be the quotient map and denote the induced tt-functor by $\alpha^*\colon \mathrm{StMod}(E,A) \to \mathrm{StMod}(E,k)$. Since $\alpha^*$ is cocontinuous, it admits a right adjoint $\alpha_*$, which in turn has a further right adjoint $\alpha_!$, see \cref{ssec:basechange}. Our goal is to apply nil-descent (\cref{thm:nildescent}) to $\alpha^*$. 

In preparation for the verification of the conditions of nil-descent, consider the localizing subcategory $\mathrm{Loc}(A) \subseteq \mathrm{StMod}(E,A)$. By derived Morita theory and \cref{prop:stmodtate}, we have an equivalence 
\[
\mathrm{Mod}(A^{tE}) \simeq \mathrm{Loc}(A),
\]
where the $E$-Tate construction is taken with respect to the trivial $E$-action on $A$. In particular, \cref{prop:elabtategeneration} transposes to the statement that $A \in \mathrm{Thick}(k)$ in $\mathrm{StMod}(E,A)$.

In particular, we see that $\alpha^*$ and $\alpha^!$ are conservative. In order to show that $\alpha_*$ is also conservative, we will use that $\mathrm{StMod}(H,k)$ is generated by the trivial $H$-representation $k$ for any finite $p$-group $H$. This yields a commutative diagram
\[
\xymatrix{\mathrm{StMod}(E,A) & \mathrm{StMod}(E,k) \ar[l]_-{\alpha_*}\\
\mathrm{Mod}(A^{tE}) \ar@{^{(}->}[u] & \mathrm{Mod}(k^{tE}) \ar[u]_{\simeq} \ar[l]^-{\alpha_*}.}
\]
The bottom horizontal map in this diagram is restriction along $\alpha\colon A^{tE}\to k^{tE}$, so it is conservative; hence the top horizontal functor is conservative as well. 

Next we show that the map $\varphi\colon \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(E,k)) \to \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(E,A))$ induced by $\alpha^*$ is bijective. To this end, recall that $\alpha^*$ is compatible with the finite localizations $\rho^*$ as in the left base-change square of \eqref{eq:rhobasechange}. The induced diagram of Balmer spectra takes the form:
\[
\xymatrix{\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(E,A)) \ar@{^{(}->}[d]_{\mathrm{Spc}(\rho^*)} & \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(E,k)) \ar@{^{(}->}[d]^{\mathrm{Spc}(\rho^*)} \ar[l]_-{\varphi} \\
\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(E,A))  & \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(E,k)). \ar[l]^-{\widetilde{\varphi}}}
\]
By Lau's theorem (\cref{thm:lau}) and naturality of Balmer's comparison map, the map $\widetilde{\varphi}$ identifies with the injection from \cref{lem:quotmapelabcohom}. It follows that $\varphi$ is injective. To see that it also surjective, note that $k$ is compact as an $A$-module, so $\mathrm{im}(\varphi) = \mathrm{supp}(\alpha_*k)$ by \cite[Thm.~1.7]{Balmer18}. Since $A \in \mathrm{Thick}(k)$, we deduce $\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(E,A)) = \mathrm{supp}(A) \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(\alpha_*k)$, which implies the claim. 

In summary, $\alpha^*$ satisfies the conditions of \cref{thm:nildescent}. We can therefore descend stratification from $\mathrm{StMod}(E,k)$, which was established in \cite{BensonIyengarKrause11a}, to the stable module category $\mathrm{StMod}(E,A)$.

The identification of the corresponding Balmer spectra is provided by \cref{thm:lau} and \cref{cor:spcstmod}, respectively. It is therefore enough to verify that $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ is stratified if and only if $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$ is stratified.

By construction, the functor $\rho^*\colon \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \to \mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ appearing in \cref{prop:mainrecollement} is a finite localization. The implication $(2) \implies (1)$ thus follows from Zariski descent (\cref{thm:zariskidescent}). 

Conversely, suppose that $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ is stratified. Write $i^*\colon \mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \to \cat D(R)$ for the symmetric monoidal forgetful functor from \cref{ssec:changeofgroups}. The corresponding base change functors $(i^*,i_*,i^!)$ together with the functors $(\rho^*,\rho_*,\rho^!)$ assemble into a triple of adjoints
\[
\xymatrix{\varphi^*=(\rho^*,i^*), \varphi^!=(\rho^!,i^!)\colon\mathrm{Rep}(G,R) \ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] & \mathrm{StMod}(G,R) \times \cat D(R) \ar[l] \nobreak \mspace{6mu plus 1mu} {:} \nonscript\mkern-\thinmuskip \mathpunct{} \mspace{2mu} \varphi_* = \rho_*\times i_*.}
\]
In other words, $\varphi^*$ has a right adjoint $\varphi_*$ which admits a further right adjoint $\varphi^! = (\rho^!,i^!)$, constructed as above. The idea is to apply nil-descent  to $\varphi^*$. 

To this end, we have to verify Conditions (a) and (b) of \cref{thm:nildescent}. We first claim that $\varphi^*$ is conservative. Indeed, suppose $\varphi^*(X) \simeq 0$ for some $X \in \mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$. By considering the first factor, we see that $X$ is in the kernel of $\rho^*$, which identifies with $\cat D(R[G])$ by \cref{prop:mainrecollement}. In light of \cref{lem:deraugconservative}, this forces $X \simeq 0$, as claimed. Similarly, consider $X$ with $\varphi^!(X)=0$. In particular, $X$ is in the kernel of $\rho^!$. By abstract local duality in the sense of \cite[Thm.~2.21]{bhv1}, this implies that $X \simeq 0$ if and only if $X \otimes R[G] \simeq 0$. But $X \otimes R[G]$ is contained in $\Loco{R[G]} \simeq \cat D(R[G])$, so we compute
\[
i^*(X \otimes R[G]) \simeq i^*(X) \otimes i^*(R[G]) \simeq i^!(X) \otimes i^*(R[G]) \simeq 0
\]
as a consequence of \cref{lem:deraugconservative}. Therefore, $X \otimes R[G] \simeq 0$ as desired.

Next, we have to verify that $\varphi_*$ is conservative, which is equivalent to saying that both $\rho_*$ and $i_*$ are conservative. In fact, $\rho_*$ is fully faithful, while the claim for $i_*$ follows from \cref{prop:restrictionetale}. We have thus verified Condition (a).

As for Condition (b), the restriction of $\varphi^*$ to compact objects induces a map on Balmer spectra
\[
\xymatrix{\mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{stmod}(G,R)) \coprod \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{Perf}(R)) \ar[r] & \mathrm{Spc}(\mathrm{rep}(G,R))}
\]
which is a spectral bijection in light of \cref{cor:spcstmod}. We are therefore in the position to apply \cref{thm:nildescent}: By assumption, $\mathrm{StMod}(G,R)$ is stratified. Since $\cat D(R)$ is stratified as well by Neeman's theorem \cite[Thm.~2.8]{Neeman92a}, stratification descends to $\mathrm{Rep}(G,R)$, as desired.

A thick subcategory cat S subseteq cat E is a full subcategory which satisfies the following closure properties: item cat S is closed under direct summands. item If 0to X to Y to Z to 0 is an exact sequence in cat E such that two terms of it are in cat S, then so is the third. For an exact category cat E which admits set-indexed coproducts, a thick subcategory of cat E is called a localizing subcategory if it is also closed under set-indexed coproducts. If cat E is additionally equipped with an exact symmetric monoidal structure otimes, we say that cat S is a thick tensor ideal or localizing tensor ideal if it is a thick subcategory or localizing subcategory which is additionally closed under otimes, respectively.
